# upwind_configuration_finding (Data Source)

Reads a single Upwind configuration (compliance) finding by ID. Findings are produced by the platform when a rule is evaluated against a resource, so they cannot be managed as a resource. This is the full record: unlike `upwind_configuration_findings`, it includes `rule.description`, `rule.remediation` and `framework.description`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A single finding by id. This is the endpoint to use when you need the rule's
# remediation text or the full resource identity, and it returns a richer
# framework object than the collection endpoint does.
#
# A finding id that does not exist is an error, not an empty result: a data source
# has no state to drop, so a missing object fails the plan.
data "upwind_configuration_finding" "public_bucket" {
  id = "cf-1a2b3c4d5e6f7890"
}

output "remediation" {
  value = {
    title       = data.upwind_configuration_finding.public_bucket.title
    severity    = data.upwind_configuration_finding.public_bucket.severity
    status      = data.upwind_configuration_finding.public_bucket.status
    resource    = data.upwind_configuration_finding.public_bucket.resource.name
    region      = data.upwind_configuration_finding.public_bucket.resource.region
    remediation = data.upwind_configuration_finding.public_bucket.rule.remediation
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the finding to read.

### Read-Only

- `evaluation_time` (String) ISO8601 timestamp of the most recent evaluation.
- `first_seen_time` (String) ISO8601 timestamp when this finding was first observed.
- `framework` (Attributes) The compliance framework the finding's rule belongs to. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--framework))
- `resource` (Attributes) The cloud resource the rule was evaluated against. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resource))
- `risk_categories` (List of String) Risk categories this finding falls under.
- `rule` (Attributes) The rule that produced this finding. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule))
- `severity` (String) Severity: `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`. Lowercase, matching configuration rules and unlike the uppercase severities on threat stories.
- `status` (String) Evaluation outcome: `pass` or `fail`. Note a finding exists for a passing check too, so filter on this rather than assuming every finding is a violation.
- `title` (String) Human-readable title of the finding.

<a id="nestedatt--framework"></a>
### Nested Schema for `framework`

Read-Only:

- `cloud_provider_name` (String) Cloud provider the framework applies to.
- `description` (String) Framework description.
- `id` (String) Framework identifier.
- `revision` (String) Framework revision.
- `status` (String) Whether the framework is `enabled` or `disabled`. A string here, though the frameworks write endpoints model the same concept as an `is_enabled` boolean.
- `title` (String) Framework title.
- `version` (String) Framework version.


<a id="nestedatt--resource"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resource`

Read-Only:

- `arn` (String) Cloud provider ARN, where the provider has one.
- `cloud_account_id` (String) Cloud account containing the resource.
- `cloud_account_name` (String) Cloud account display name.
- `cloud_provider_name` (String) One of `aws`, `gcp`, `azure`, `oracle`, or `byoc`.
- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster identifier, for Kubernetes resources.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier.
- `name` (String) Resource name.
- `namespace` (String) Namespace, for Kubernetes resources.
- `region` (String) Cloud region.
- `sync_time` (String) ISO8601 timestamp when Upwind last synced the resource.
- `type` (String) Resource type, e.g. `aws_s3_bucket`.
- `upwind_asset_id` (String) Upwind's own asset identifier.


<a id="nestedatt--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Read-Only:

- `description` (String) What the rule checks.
- `id` (String) Rule identifier.
- `remediation` (String) How to remediate a failing resource.
- `title` (String) Rule title.
